articles.title: Tai Chi Symbol and Tai Chi Yin Yang Symbol
articles.summary: Tai Chi Chuan is one of the excellences of traditional Chinese culture. There exist, however, many mistaken concepts and much confusing information about it that mislead everyone who seeks to understand Tai Chi Chuan and that also interferes with its development.
articles.content:
I. Introduction

Tai Chi Chuan is one of the excellences of traditional Chinese culture. There exist, however, many mistaken concepts and much confusing information about it that mislead everyone who seeks to understand Tai Chi Chuan and that also interferes with its development. Tai Chi Chuan is based on the information presented in the Tai Chi Symbol—so what is the genuine Tai Chi Symbol? Is there a difference between the Tai Chi Symbol and the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol? Are Tai Chi philosophy and Yin and Yang philosophy the same?

Even most Chinese today do not understand the answers to these questions. Due to confusing the basic philosophies and concepts, there are many people who mistakenly assume the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is the Tai Chi Symbol, who draw a circle to represent a “Wu Chi Symbol,” and who substitute Yin and Yang philosophy for Tai Chi philosophy. There are many Tai Chi Chuan organizations that use the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol (commonly called the “Yin and Yang Symbol”) for their organizations’ logo, and there are many people who explain their Tai Chi Chuan teaching solely with Yin and Yang philosophy.

Tai Chi philosophy and the Tai Chi Symbol are the building blocks for Tai Chi Chuan; they are the reason Tai Chi Chuan was formulated and transmitted. How to properly explain Tai Chi Chuan philosophy and how to better propagate Tai Chi Chuan should be the primary objectives of all Tai Chi Chuan teachers and enthusiasts. In the broad field that is Tai Chi Chuan, its philosophy, research, application, and correcting mistakes concerning Tai Chi Symbol—all of these need our immediate attention and solution.

II. The Information for Tai Chi Philosophy

Tai Chi Chuan Treatise author Wang Tsung Yueh (1525-1606) wrote, “Tai Chi came from Wu Chi and is the mother of Yin and Yang. When it is in motion, it separates. When it is not in motion, it combines.” Tai Chi philosophy is part of traditional Chinese philosophy. It is the earliest philosophy used by ancient Chinese in researching and understanding the origin and the transformation of the material universe. The concept of Tai Chi originated very early in Chinese history. It can trace to the Xia (2033-1562 B.C.E.) and Shang (1562-1066 B.C.E.) Dynasties or perhaps earlier. The Tai Chi philosophy was slowly formulated from the ancient Chinese’s understanding of nature and society. What followed was the slow process of enriching the definition of the Tai Chi philosophy as it became a mature philosophy. Cao Duan in the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) wrote in The Explanation of the Tai Chi Symbol, “Tai Chi refers to heaven, earth, and humanity; these three concepts have qi and form; the name for the Chaos is not determined.” Over time it was applied in politics, the military, economics, culture, and martial arts. Later, when martial arts combined with this philosophy, it led to the formation of Tai Chi Chuan.

Within traditional Chinese philosophy, there are the Wu Chi philosophy, Tai Chi philosophy, Bagua Diagram philosophy, Yin and Yang Theory philosophy, and Wuxing Five Element Theory philosophy, among others. Tai Chi philosophy is one of the major philosophies in Chinese culture for understanding and explaining the formation of the universe. It is also an important philosophical source for understanding and practicing Tai Chi Chuan today. Tai Chi philosophy is centered on Tai Chi conditions; it includes Wu Chi philosophy and Yin and Yang philosophy, the complete system of traditional Chinese philosophy.

A. Wu Chi Philosophy

The term Wu Chi first appeared in the book called Lao Tzu written in the Spring and Autumn Period (770-476 BCE): “When the eternal dao and De [virtue] are no longer have any difference, they will return to Wu Chi.” What is Wu Chi? Cao Duan wrote, “Wu refers to no form, no phenomenon, no sound, and no direction. Chi refers to extreme and is another name for reason.” Reason is defined as having no form to observe, no sound to listen to, and no direction to indicate. It is completely filled and solid. What is needed to make clear in this discussion is this: Wu Chi does not mean “the void” or “no object”; it means “no form” and “no limit.” It signifies the stage of no limit for material things. Also, it does not represent the philosophies of Two Elements, Four Phenomena, Wuxing Five Elements Theory philosophy, and Bagua Diagram added together. It indicates the beginning stage of unlimited material things, or the beginning of material things. Ancient Chinese philosophers concluded that Wu Chi was the beginning of the universe. Later, people elaborated this idea further: “It is the embryo of Tai Chi; it is the originator of nothingness; the root of Chaos. It is the great emptiness that cannot be measured by a ruler. It is open space so wide that one cannot see the shore. It is so big that there is no outside. It is so small that there is no space inside. It is so big it includes heaven and earth. It is so small inside that no light can penetrate. It is difficult to give it a proper name.” Therefore, Wu Chi has no trait and trace, and no diagram can demonstrate this characteristic.

Today, in the martial arts and qigong communities, there is a Wu Chi Symbol: a simple circle. What this Wu Chi Symbol indicates is that the people who draw it have a shallow understanding of Wu Chi philosophy. It misinterprets the multiple entities as a single entity, and a no-form and no-phenomenon entity as one having form and phenomenon. What results is misinterpreting Tai Chi Chuan’s pre-heaven natural features as post-heaven manmade features, and Tai Chi Chuan’s superior reverse-order training for returning to natural conditions becomes an inferior training that exhausts one’s energy and spirit. In addition, there are people who misinterpret pioneer Neo-Confucianist philosopher Zhou Dun Yi’s Tai Chi Transformation Symbol (fig. 1) (It has five levels. Starts from the top, the 1st level is Tai Chi came from Wu Chi; the 2nd level is Yang dynamic condition and Yin static condition; 3rd level is the Five Elements came from Yin and Yang; the 4th level is humanity came from Yin and Yang; the 5th level is the creation of ten thousand things) as a symbol for Wu Chi (fig. 2) (It has five levels. Start from the bottom, the 1st level is the beginning; the 2nd level is transforming the essence to qi then transforming the qi to spirit; the 3rd level is establishment of the Wuxing (Five Elements); the 4th level is Yin and Yang complement; the 5th level is transforming the \ to nothingness or returning to Wu Chi). This is a big mistake. These mistakes all result from a lack of information on Wu Chi philosophy.

B. Tai Chi philosophy

The term Tai Chi first appeared in the Zhou Yi Jing during the early Western Zhou Dynasty (1066-771 B.C.E.): “It has Tai Chi, bears Two Elements.” The original meaning of Tai Chi referred to the most important, biggest and tallest. In the Ci Hai Dictionary it says, “Tai refers to bigger than big.” In another dictionary, Shou Wen Jie Zi wrote, “People from later generations used this word (tai) for everything that is bigger than big.” In Zhou Zi Quan Shu, Tu Shuo wrote, “Chi refers to the highest point in the house.”

The earliest application of the term Tai Chi was for a concept to describe a specific universal phenomenon: it was a manifestation coming from Wu Chi. The concept of Tai Chi included qi energy. Therefore, Tai Chi has the feature of transformation. Transformation means change. When Tai Chi is under the function of transformation, it becomes an entity with two elements. This is the obvious difference between Wu Chi and Tai Chi. The two elements refer to heaven and earth. It is the fundamental formation of the universe. This is the beginning of the concept of Yin and Yang. Therefore, one can see that Tai Chi, as a concept, lies in between Wu Chi and Yin and Yang. Zhou Dun Yi (1017-1073) wrote in his book Tai Chi Tu Shuo (“The Explanation of the Tai Chi Symbol”), “Wu Chi then Tai Chi, Tai Chi active bears Yang. After extremely active then becomes inactive. Inactive bears Yin. After extreme inactive than repeats active again, it is continuing in this fashion. Yin and Yang are the roots of each other. When there is Yin and Yang, there is the establishment of two elements.”

Tai Chi is called the highest Dao. It has the ability to transform into Yin and Yang, the source of the creation of all material things. Xu Yu Sheng (1878-1945) referred to Tai Chi as the “opportunity crossroads for Yin and Yang.” When the universe is transformed from Wu Chi to Tai Chi, the universe is transformed from a condition of chaos to a condition of visible order in which everything is manifested and created. On the other hand, when the visible-entity universe is transformed back to Wu Chi, material things cease to exist. This is the important information of Tai Chi. When Tai Chi moves, it has the ability to move in an active direction as well as in the direction of inactivity. This is the meaning of, “when it is active, it separates; when it is inactive, it combines.” The separation referred to here is the formation of two elements: the appearance of Yin and Yang at their simplest stage. The combination referred to is the disappearance of two elements, the stage of chaos. The Tai Chi chaotic condition is the phenomenon of the specific Wu Chi condition. It is the condition of storing qi. The key to Tai Chi’s active and inactive transformations is that they rely on the condition of extremes. When active is in an extreme condition, it becomes inactive. When inactive is in an extreme condition, it becomes active. It is due to this feature (transformation happening at extreme stages) that the creation, movement, and transformation of material things happens.

I have to point out that Wu Chi is the extreme of inactive and that Yin and Yang is the extreme of active and that Tai Chi is in the middle between these two extremes. The transformation of Tai Chi can happen in a long time or a short time. When it is a slow transformation, it lasts a long time. When it is an extreme transformation, it happens in a moment. In other words, the extreme-active and extreme-inactive transformations can happen in a second or can last a long time.

Tai Chi’s transformation in either an active or inactive direction does not follow any specific rule. It follows whatever opportunity is present at the moment. Therefore, it appears to be very mysterious and unpredictable. Cao Duan called this, “Tai Chi, it is a wonder of nature. It has Yin and Yang. Active and inactive directions both follow the opportunity. It has no limit.”

Tai Chi’s transformational directions are called the “opportunity crossroads.” The creation and product of these two directional transformations appear to be in a “spiral turning motion.” In Tai Chi Chuan, the form of the yielding technique also appears to be a “spiral turning motion.” This spiral turning motion has no beginning and no end. This is called, “active and inactive are infinite”: separation and combination without end.

Tai Chi is the root of all material things that are created. It is the key for the beginning and ending of all things, and the success or failure of all things. Therefore, it is called Tai Chi. If not the name Tai Chi, then what is the proper name?

C. Yin and Yang Philosophy

The term Yin and Yang also first appeared in the book Zhou Yi Jing (zhou’s book of changes). It says, “One Yin and one Yang is called Dao.” Originally, the meaning of Yin and Yang was very simple. It referred to in front of or behind the sunlight. In front of the sunlight, it is bright and so it is called Yang; behind the sunlight, it is dark and so it is called Yin. Therefore, the sun is called “extreme Yang” and the moon is called “extreme Yin.” Subsequently, due to Yin and Yang’s features of opposition, complementarity, and balance, the concept was applied in ancient society in many areas, and descriptive terms such as dynamic and static, hard and soft, up and down, advance and retreat, hot and cold, fast and slow, etc. were used to distinguish and explain Yin and Yang’s oppositional and complementary features. In this way, the function of Yin and Yang as a basic concept applying to material things entered into a category of ancient philosophy. When the definition of Yin and Yang became further enriched and completed, developing into Yin and Yang interaction and Yin and Yang counteraction, it separated from being merely a category of Tai Chi philosophy and became established as a philosophy by itself.

Due to the fact that all things and phenomena have the characteristics of opposition and unity, this universal principle of Yin and Yang duality, which includes both opposition, complementarity and interaction, applies to and exists in all things. The Yin and Yang feature in all material things is complementary, not absolute. This is the special feature of “one separating into two.” According to this special feature, everything that is on top, warm, bright, outside, etc. belongs to the category of Yang. Everything that is on the bottom, cold, dark, inside, etc. belongs to the category of Yin. This special feature cannot be easily changed. Yin and Yang Theory in Tai Chi philosophy is the basis of Yin and Yang philosophy. Yin and Yang philosophy is the in-depth completion of Yin and Yang Theory. The application of Yin and Yang philosophy in the art of Tai Chi Chuan is confined solely to Yin and Yang Theory. The reason is that the primary emphasis of a martial art is not on philosophy; it is on, or should be on, how to execute the technique—physical movement. Philosophy is emphasized solely as a function to better guide the training of the physical movement, so the quality will become better. Therefore, the nucleus of Tai Chi Chuan training should be based on Tai Chi philosophy, not Yin and Yang philosophy. This is why it is called Tai Chi Chuan and not Yin and Yang Chuan.

The root and requirement of Yin and Yang formation is movement. Yin and Yang is extreme active movement. Without any movement, there is no Yin and Yang. Within this Yin and Yang formation, the Yin component has the meaning of inactive. This inactive is in a dynamic condition of being opposite to the active. It is different from the inactive of Wu Chi. The inactive in Wu Chi is extreme inactive, also called the “condition of chaos.” In addition, the active and inactive qualities in Yin and Yang philosophy have a visible boundary. It is “post-heaven” and has form. Wu Chi has no active and inactive separation. Therefore, there is no boundary. It is “pre-heaven” and has no form.

There are many people who assume that Tai Chi and Yin and Yang are the same thing; they assume Tai Chi has the same meaning and features as Yin and Yang. Therefore, these people assume each Tai Chi Chuan movement has one technique and has the same Yin and Yang feature. Therefore, it is called Tai Chi Chuan. The result is to mislead and confuse people concerning the difference between Tai Chi and Yin and Yang. The feature of Yin and Yang duality exists in all things in nature. Tai Chi Chuan techniques possess this duality—as do all Chinese martial arts techniques. Can you call all martial arts Tai Chi Chuan? In this world, all things have this property of duality. If a martial-arts style has this Yin and Yang feature, if every technique cannot be separated from this Yin and Yang feature, then this style should be called Yin and Yang Chuan, not Tai Chi Chuan. If it is called Tai Chi Chuan, the style should be mandated by the Tai Chi philosophy.

III. The Formation of the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol and the Tai Chi Symbol

A symbol is the abstract of information gained by direct observation. It is straightforward and the simplest way to present this information. Tai Chi philosophy presents the formation and evolution of the universe, and Yin and Yang philosophy presents the basic rule of the operation of all things. In ancient China, people used numbers—mathematics—to represent natural phenomena, used natural phenomena to analyze philosophy, and used philosophy to develop a unique system of culture. The philosophy of Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol and Yin and Yang Symbol came from Hetu Mathematical Diagram, “The Yellow River Map” (fig. 3) and Luoshui Mathematical Diagram. “The Writing from the River Luo” (fig. 4). In the book Yi Jing it says, “The map came from Hetu Mathematical Diagram and the book came from Luoshui Mathematical Diagram. It was spoken by the sage.” Therefore, the map that came from the Hetu Mathematical Diagram and the book that came from the Luoshui Mathematical Diagram form the beginning of Chinese culture.

A. The Original Tai Chi Symbol

The production of the Tai Chi Symbol originated from the Hetu Mathematical Diagram, which can be traced to ancient times. The legend says that Fu Xi Shi, a prehistoric tribal leader, saw a beast with these mathematical markings surfacing at the Yellow River. Therefore, this mathematical diagram is called Hetu Mathematical Diagram (fig. 3). The Neo-Confucianist philosopher Zhu Xi in the Song Dynasty (960-1279 CE) believed, “It is numbers that speak of heaven and earth. Yang refers to the odd numbers and Yin refers to the even numbers. It is called the Hetu Mathematical Diagram.”

Although this mathematical diagram consists of numbers, it has a unique arrangement of the numbers. In the diagram, the white colored numbers represent Yang and the dark numbers represent Yin. It has the following arrangement: one and six at the bottom; three and eight on the left; two and seven on the top; four and nine on the right; and five at the center. The difference between each set of numbers is five. The mathematical diagram corresponding to the Tai Chi Symbol comes from the Hetu Mathematical Diagram. In the mathematical diagram, if we use dots to represent numbers and connect all the Yang dots with a broken line and the Yin dots with a straight line (fig. 5), the mathematical diagram will end up as a spiral (fig. 6a,6b). The broken line initiates with the Yang numbers and connects all the Yang numbers; it represents the Yang component. The straight line initiates with the Yin numbers and connects all the Yin numbers; it represents the Yin component. With Yang represented by the white color and Yin represented by the black color, then we have the diagram of the Tai Chi Symbol (fig. 7). The white circle at the center is the Tai Chi original entity. It is the inactive part of the diagram; it has Yin and Yang together. Outside this white circle is the active part. It is separated into Yin and Yang. This means: potential is inside and realization is outside. This symbol presents the secret of “active and inactive opportunity.”

B. The Formation of the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol

The Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol came from the Luoshui Mathematical Diagram (fig. 4). The legend goes that when Yu, a tribal leader, was managing the floodwater at the Yellow River in the area called Luoshui, or Luo River, a turtle carrying a mathematical configuration with nine numbers on its back surfaced. Yu, the same tribal leader, who defeated all the neighboring tribes and formed the first feudal kingdom, called the Xia Dynasty (2100-1800 BC; his subjects called him Yu Wang—“King Yu”), made a mathematical diagram based on it. The arrangement of this mathematical diagram is as follows: “weaving the nine and stepping on the one; three is on the left and seven is on the right; two and four are the shoulders; six and eight are the feet; and five is at the center.” The rules are that the odd or Yang numbers are located at the four directions and the even or Yin numbers are located at the four corners. The two opposite numbers added together are equal to ten. In the mathematical diagram, use dots to represent the numbers and connect all the Yang numbers to form a backward S shape (fig. 8). Draw a circle around this S shape to represent a complete entity (fig. 9). The curved line divides the circle into two equal parts to form two elements (fig. 10). When the Two Elements philosophy evolved it became the Yin and Yang philosophy. In the mathematical diagram, the fish eyes appear in extreme Yin and extreme Yang to represent that there is a Yin component within the Yang component and there is a Yang component within the Yin component. This is the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol (fig. 11).

IV. The Difference between the Tai Chi Symbol and the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol

The Tai Chi Symbol and the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol are very different. We can comprehend their difference in the following eight areas.

A. Formation

Tai Chi came from Wu Chi. Yin and Yang is the product when Tai Chi is active.

B. Meaning

Tai Chi is a universal phenomenon that existed before the creation of heaven and earth. Yin and Yang represents a duality principle of opposite and complementary characteristics that applies to any material thing.

C. Type of Movement

In Tai Chi, when it is active, it becomes two elements. When it is inactive, it returns to Wu Chi. In Yin and Yang, when it is active, it is complementary and balanced. When it is inactive, it is opposites.

D. Characteristics of Movement

Tai Chi has active and inactive opportunities. It has equal opportunity developing in both directions. Yin and Yang, on the other hand, has only one active option: to neutralize each other to become balanced.

E. Method of Active and Inactive

In Tai Chi, after it reaches the extreme active condition, it will return to inactive. When it reaches the extreme inactive condition, it will return to active again. With Yin and Yang, they have each other: the active has the inactive component and the inactive has the active component at all times.

F. Function

Tai Chi is the key to the creation of all material things. Yin and Yang is the basic composition of all material things.

G. Application in Martial Arts

Tai Chi is the guide for the principles behind Tai Chi Chuan’s mind intention and qi circulation training. Yin and Yang is the guide for the principle behind Tai Chi Chuan’s physical-training. Mind-intent and qi circulation are the essence of Tai Chi Chuan training.

H. Formation of the Tai Chi Symbol and the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol

The Tai Chi Symbol came from the Hetu Mathematical Diagram. The Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol came from the Luoshui Mathematical Diagram. The presentations from the Tai Chi Symbol and the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol are completely different. Therefore, one should not mix them up. One cannot substitute one for the other.

V. Conclusion

Due to a basic misunderstanding, there are many people who mistake the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol for the Tai Chi Symbol. Thus, it is not just the knowledge of Tai Chi’s inactive transformation that gets lost, but, most importantly, it is the information that Tai Chi has “active and inactive opportunity” that gets lost. It is the result of this misunderstanding that in today’s Tai Chi Chuan there is often a strong emphasis on the physical Yin and Yang training without any mind intention and qi circulation training and application. Because of this neglect, what was originally an advanced and profound martial art with mind intention and qi circulation training became a low level martial art with an emphasis solely on the physical movement.

Due to this basic misunderstanding, the appearance of the Tai Chi Symbol in the martial arts and qigong communities has become very confusing, mainly in the following three areas:

A. The assumption that the Tai Chi inactive condition diagram is the Wu Chi Diagram.

B. The assumption that the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is the Tai Chi Symbol.

C. Ignorance of the true Tai Chi Symbol.

The confusion directly reflects people’s understanding of the Tai Chi philosophy. This limits the development of Tai Chi Chuan. Tai Chi Chuan should rely primarily on Tai Chi philosophy for its guide and the Yin and Yang Theory for its secondary guide. Therefore, one should apply the information or philosophy in the Tai Chi Symbol to represent its philosophy. It is time to make it right again. It is only when applying the correct philosophy to guide Tai Chi Chuan that it can be called the genuine Tai Chi Chuan.

articles.title: Tai Chi Yin Yang Symbol and Tai Chi Chuan
articles.summary: The ancient Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol came from the mathematical diagram of Hetu Mathematical Diagram. It has nine major informational contributions to Tai Chi Chuan practice.
articles.content:
I. Introduction

The ancient Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol came from the mathematical diagram of Hetu Mathematical Diagram. It has nine major informational contributions to Tai Chi Chuan practice. Due to its contribution to Tai Chi Chuan’s principles and practice, Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol mistakenly called Tai Chi Symbol. The symbol is simple. It is but a circle divided into two equal black and white portions by a wavy line. Inside the black portion has a white dot and inside the white portion has a black dot. These two black and white portions are known as black and white fishes and the black and white dots are known as fish eyes. The symbol reveals the duality property and principle of all things in nature. Tai Chi Chuan developed at the peak of Chinese martial art development. It has an unique feature that is different from the traditional Chinese martial art that people called it as the internal Chinese martial art. Most of the people recognized it as a soft, slow, relaxed, circular and steady movement and philosophical martial art. It is one of the most popular physical activities that people practice world wide today. The Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol and Tai Chi Chuan have a very close relationship. The Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is provided the Tai Chi Chuan with philosophical principle how to practice and Tai Chi Chuan is provided the physical interpretation of the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol's philosophy.

From its appearance, Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is but a circle. Inside the circle is composed of two interchangeable Yin and Yang fishes connecting together in the infinite process of Yin and Yang transformation. This is the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol. Tai Chi Chuan is based on the information from this circle, better known as Tai Chi philosophy. Therefore, every Tai Chi Chuan movement is circular. It does not matter the movement is inside or outside, left or right, and up or down, it is not separate from this circle. In Tai Chi Chuan practices, everyone movement should adhere to this circle. The activity should not have any deficiencies and no excesses. It should be continued without any pause or sudden choppiness. This is similar to the ocean waves. One tide come after another in a non-stop process. When one conducts the Tai Chi Chuan movements, opening and closing motions, empty and full body weight, breathing in and out, and top and bottom coordination, must have active and inactive harmony, Yin and Yang harmony, mind intention and physical movement harmony, Yang has Yin value and Yin has Yang value, empty has full value and full has empty value, hard power has soft power and soft power has hard power value, and inactive has active value and active has inactive value at all time and they all are not separate from this circle. Circle means alive.

II. Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol’s Features Contributed to Tai Chi Chuan practice

Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is a simple and complex symbol. It demonstrated the common rule among all things in this world. The symbol has the following information: it has opposition and complement; one becomes two and two combined into one; it has slow changes and sudden changes; it has quantity changes and quality changes; it has inclusiveness and exclusiveness; it has extreme large and extreme small, it has reason and result; it has tangible and intangible. One can see, symbol has plenty information. Therefore, it is the basic building block for many traditional Chinese cultures. Traditional Chinese medicine considered it as a systemic illustration. Qigong practitioners considered it as an alchemy illustration. Painters called it as the secret of paining. Tai Chi Chuan practitioners called it as the secret of Tai Chi Chuan. It has nine features relating to Tai Chi Chuan practice. They are integral body, three dimensional circular body, Yin and Yang opposition, Yin and Yang within each other, Yin and Yang complementarity, Yin and Yang spiral transformation, reversing order, centrifugal and centripetal forces and Yin and Yang balance.

1. Integral Body

The first feature in Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is about wholeness or completeness. It is often represented by a simple circle. Chinese culture has a different approach than the western culture when come to studying and exploration. Chinese culture always begins from a completeness of an entity while western culture always begins with an individual part of an entity. When one is studying the subject in a completeness entity, one has an overview what to expect and the relationship among different components to make it as a completeness entity

Tai Chi Chuan practice is a continuation of this completeness and beauty representation. Therefore, in Tai Chi Chuan practice, it has the requirements of “The entire body move as one unit”, “integrative power”, “when one part moves, all parts move together”, “when the waist not moves, the hands should not move”, “when the inside attributes not move, the outside attributes should not move”, “inside and outside harmony”, and “upper and lower body coordination”. This integral bodily movement is one of the major distinctions between Tai Chi Chuan from other Chinese martial arts. In our daily activity, we often conducted activity in partial body involvement. For example, we want to drink some water by pick up the glass with the hands. We can do it by sitting down without the lower body’s involvement. This is not possible with Tai Chi Chuan practice. It does not matter a movement is big or small, the movement must initialize from the waist and involve the entire body in Tai Chi Chuan practice. The same requirement applies to Tai Chi Chuan push-hands exercise as well. The Tai Chi Chuan Classics written “lead the opponent’s strike to come forward to miss the target than one will follow-up with a combination force to counter strike.” Combination force is referred to the power generated from body integration. This is the difficulty of Tai Chi Chuan practice, to attain body integration. It is the same reason why one witnesses Tai Chi Chuan practice in soft, slow and relaxed manner with circular motion. In order to attain body integration, the body movement has to initial from the waist, not the hands, is the basic requirement and follow with many repetitions until the body’s inside and outside elements recognized the mechanic of the movement and act together accordingly.

2. A Three-dimensional Circular Body

The second feature from the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is circle or circular motion. It is not simply a one-dimensional circle. Rather, it is a three-dimensional circle that has top, bottom, left and right sides. Keeping with this meaning in mind, when one practices the Tai Chi Chuan solo form, the entire body is moving in circular motion without any stop. The Tai Chi Chuan Classics described this as “Internal qi is circulated and external qi is full.” Therefore, a movement has hidden and potential ward-off jin power technique at any part of the body. This is why any body part contacts the opponent can be apply as weapon to strike. Although Tai Chi Chuan has eight major hand techniques of ward-off, roll back, press, push, pull down, split, elbow strike and shoulder strike, actually, they are but variations of the ward-off technique based on its application. One of the objectives in Tai Chi Chuan practice is about qi circulation to have the qi fills up the body (sphere) like a balloon with air and this filled up qi body has buoyancy and spiral motion features. Through practice the Tai Chi Chuan solo form, one is capable to have substantial and insubstantial transformation done quickly while one is maintaining balance.

Why the Tai Chi Chuan Classics is emphasized on opening the groin? It is to enhance the lower body condition to establish better stability, circular and spiral motions when one is conducted substantial and insubstantial transformation on the feet. Therefore, if one practices Tai Chi Chuan correctly, the body is filled up with qi as a sphere moving in a spiral motion to generated the centrifugal and centripetal forces with one speedy balancing center. We knew a person is generally had two balancing centers with two feet standing up. One may ask, how is it possible to have one balancing center? It is possible if one is able to develop and have substantial and insubstantial transformation skill and ability. This is the reason why that throughout the Tai Chi Chuan solo form practice, the practitioner’s body is always balance on one foot. It is to develop this skill and ability. It is the same reason when Yang Cheng fu (1883-1936) asked for substantial and substantial has to be well differentiated in one of his Ten Points of practice. This ability is referred to as the power of center equilibrium in Tai Chi Chuan vocabulary. It is the last principle of the 13 principles or 13 postures (ward-off, roll-back, press, push, pull-down, split, elbow-strike, shoulder-strike, advance, retreat, left, right and center equilibrium). When one has this skill and ability, one is able to change the direction quickly without hurtful oneself. Therefore, one is very mobile in confrontational engagement. The Tai Chi Chuan Classics described this as “In action the whole body should be nimble and connected; The qi is better when it is circulating; The spirit should be confined within. There should be no deficiencies and no excesses, no pauses or sudden choppiness.”

3. Yin and Yang Opposition

The third feature one can see in the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is that a symbol has two equal portions referred to as Yin and Yang fishes. These two components are opposite and complement to each other. The ancient book of Yi Jing (book of changes) revealed that everything in nature has Yin and Yang components duality property and principle. This Yin and Yang components duality property and principle relay on each other to survive and support in a single entity. One of the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol features is a reflection of this information. There is an ancient philosophical concept, “one Yin and one Yang is the Dao” revealed that everything is manifested from Yin and Yang components interaction. When people are thinking and learning about something or object, they always begin with Yin and Yang opposition and complementarity components, the basic building blocks. It is so much easier to understand or to learn if one begins with the basic. Opposition and complementarity are the basic rule of nature. It is also the highest rule in Tai Chi Chuan practice. Zheng San Feng, the patron saint of Tai Chi Chuan said that Yin and Yang components are the establishment of Tai Chi phenomenon. If one does not understand this information, one is not his student. Therefore, in Tai Chi Chuan practice, it is common to observe the movements have hard and soft power, opening and closing motions, substantial and insubstantial transformation, and fast and slow motion. The opposite and complement principles will make the body equally exercise, better coordinated and balance. The same principle applies to accumulation and discharging powers as well.

4. Yin and Yang Within Each Other

The fourth feature in the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is the black fish has white eye and the white fish has black eye. This means there is Yin element in Yang component and there is Yang element in Yin component. In other others, Yin and Yang is the root of their opposition and it has the meaning of infinite divisional process. This is a very unique distribution. Therefore, martial art practitioners considered this is a perfect distribution and go as far as to recommend one should have hard and soft components in each technique to be effective and powerful because absolute hard is easily to break and absolute soft is easily to collapse. Therefore, absolute hard and absolute soft is not good. We often observe the similar recommendation in Tai Chi Chuan practice as well. In every opening motion, there should be some elements of closing. In a closing motion, there should be some elements of opening, clearly defined substantial and insubstantial transformation, hard and soft power application and fast and slow motion, etc.

5. Yin and Yang Complementarity

The fifth feature in the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is that the bigger part of the Yin fish is the smaller part of the Yang fish (Yin fish head is corresponding to the Yang fish tail and Yang fish head is corresponding to the Yin fish tail). The bigger part of the Yang fish is the smaller part of the Yin fish. Yin and Yang are complemented to each other.

The book of Yi Jing explained this as the nature of things in their dynamic condition. When the first part is advancing, the second part is retreating, a phenomenon to provide balance and stable condition with quality transformation. In Tai Chi Chuan practice, one should correctly apply this information to practice, especially so with Tai Chi Chuan push-hands exercise operation. It is only when one correctly applied this information to practice than one is able to launch multiple techniques in offense or defense. One will not lose in competition.

In Tai Chi Chuan practice, one witnesses this Yin and Yang complementarity everywhere. It is from substantial and insubstantial transformations, quantity and quality transformations, advancing and retreating engagement tactics, left and right strikes, top and below strikes, ascending and descending body manipulations, etc.

6. Yin and Yang Spiral Transformation

The sixth feature from Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is about a wavy line or a divider. It represents the division is a dynamic condition, not a constant condition. This is referred to all the transformations are happened in a spiral dynamic transforming and developing. Tai Chi Chuan movements and practice are utilized the bodily joints so the movements are always in slow and circular or spiral motion, not happen in a straight line. This spiral motion is so steady with control that some practitioners described it as pulling silk from a cocoon. When the motion is slow and steady, the delicate tendons, ligaments and muscles at the joints are properly exercised, stretched and lubricated. A necessary quality to support martial art activity. If the motion is fast, the delicate tendons, ligaments and muscles at the joints can easily cause injury. Of cause, if the bodily joints exercised regularly, they will become so flexible and strong that one can move quickly for martial art application. Since most of the people are born with the body and bodily joints are not really for martial art vigorous activity, it is better for one to begin martial art training with the objective to improve the condition of the body condition and bodily joints. Chinese martial art called this training program the Yi Jin Gong.

7. Reverse-Order

In addition, this wavy line divider is also referred to as the opportunity crossroads. It means that it can start from or heading into both directions. The two directions are Wu Chi and Two Elements (Yin and Yang). The active direction is the Two Elements and the inactive direction is the Wu Chi. Since one Yin and one Yang is Dao, Lao Tzu described it in Dao De Jing as “the Dao is developed in its reverse-order”. This method of reverse-order development is followed nature and followed the principle of “when it developed to its extreme, it will be transformed to its opposition” as explained in the book of Yi Jing. Based on this principle, there are many traditional Chinese cultures observed this principle. A closer look at the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol, a wavy line divider demonstrated a similar meaning. It does not matter it is transforming from large to small direction or from small to large direction, they are begun with the reverse-order, We observed similar transformation in Tai Chi Chuan practice. In order to move the left hand, it is beginning to move with the right hand. To move the right hand, it is beginning with to move the left hand. To move the hands, it is beginning with to move the feet. To conduct a opening motion, it is beginning to conduct a closing motion first. To conduct a closing motion, it is beginning with an opening motion, etc. This phenomenon literary written as bending and stockpile in the Tai Chi Chuan Classics. It is commonly known as folding or zip-zap motion by the contemporary Tai Chi Chuan practitioners. It is so important that it has perfect mechanical motion to train for body balance, improve qi and blood circulation among the physiologic organs and their functions, for qi accumulation and power discharging technical merits, expressing the rhythmic motion beauty and interpreting the Yin and Yang duality features.

8. Centrifugal Force and Centripetal Force

The eighth feature in Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is about its fish eyes. If we focus on the Yin fish eye, the Yin fish is moving in a centripetal direction and the fish tail is produced centrifugal force. If we focus on the Yang fish eye, the Yang fish is moving in a centrifugal direction and the fish tail is produced centripetal force. Centrifugal and centripetal forces are two opposite forces in nature. In Tai Chi Chuan practice, it makes the two opposite forces work together as one unit. We observed this information applying in Tai Chi Chuan techniques all the time with profundity. It is the supporting source of the principle for four ounces overcome a thousand pounds. It is an unique feature of Yin and Yang components work together.

9. Yin and Yang Balance

The ninth feature in the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is the Yin and Yang fishes are existed together in one entity. This Yin and Yang balance explained in the book of Yi Jing as the originator of all things. When Yin and Yang come together, it interacts and produces. If Yin and Yang cannot come together, it is separated and death. When a philosopher said that Yin and Yang produced 10000 things, it is the function and demonstration of this Yin and Yang balance and interaction. Yin and Yang balance is a vibrant and dynamic condition. Therefore, Tai Chi Chuan practice is a process of balancing the body’s Yin and Yang components. It is a process of balancing the body’s different physiologic organs and their functions. The result is a healthy body.

One can see, if one is solely focus the Tai Chi Chuan practices on the physical movements and ignored all the internal attributes, it is not a correct practice and it is not possible to balance the body’s Yin and Yang components. It yields no benefit to the body and health.

One can see, although Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is a simple symbol, it has many hidden information. In order to improve one’s Tai Chi Chuan skill, it is necessary for one to invest the time to study this ancient simple symbol well and incorporate the information to one’s Tai Chi Chuan practice.

III. The Relationship Between Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol and Tai Chi Chuan

Although Tai Chi Chuan is not created based on animals’ features as many Chinese martial art systems do, the creation and practice were contributed, inspired and credited from the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol's philosophy. Practicing the Tai Chi Chuan movements are based on the information from the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol and others to conducted circle and circular motions by involving the bodily joints. Circle represents beauty, perfection, agility, nature and transformation. Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is a completeness, circle and beautiful symbol. It has the meaning of harmony, unity and balance. They are the essences of Chinese philosophy. The symbol reveals to the public that people should pay attention to the completion, harmony and balance when come to find solution for any subject, question and issue that one will confront in daily life. One found the same philosophy applying in Tai Chi Chuan practice as well. For example, "Body integration"; "When one part moves, all parts should move together." and "The power has to be integrated." All three quotations came from the Tai Chi Chuan Classics reflected the unity in body trainings and requirements one should aim. Unity is the result of coordination between internal and external attributes in the body. The aiming revealed the function of unity capable to maintain balance and the ability to solidify the body balancing center.

Inside the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol, the two Yin and Yang fishes represent the Yin and Yang two elements are separated by the wavy line. The white fish represents Yang element and dynamic condition. It is represented heaven. In Tai Chi Chuan practice, it is represented hard power, full body weight, above and advancing movements, etc. The black fish represents Yin element and static condition. It is represented earth. In Tai Chi Chuan practice, it is represented soft power, empty body weight, below and retreating movements, etc. Among the Yin and Yang Fishes in the symbol, the formation for one fish is from big to small. The formation for the second fish is from small to big. The head for one fish is connected to the tail of the other fish to form a wonderful and beautiful symbol. This symbol indicated the infinite dynamic spiral transformation condition of Yin and Yang opposition, complementarity and balance situations existing in the same time and space. The symbol introduced the following principles in Tai Chi Chuan practice as the same moment with equal contribution from both Yin and Yang components: Opening and closing are together; empty and full are interchangeable; hard and soft are interacting, fast and slow speed are steady and proper; adhesive and separation are complemented each other; when heading to the top, be ware the bottom; when advancing forward, be ware of retreating and when retreating, be aware of advancing. The separation of Yin and Yang fishes is by a wavy line. This wavy line strongly suggested that the separation is not a clear and smooth separation but very bumpy. In Tai Chi Chuan practice, this information is interpreted as applying the uncommon act of waist rotation to make all kinds of transitional movements and followed with the limbs’ movements.

IV. Yin and Yang Transformation Associate with Tai Chi Chuan

The Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol is a completeness and beautiful circle. Two fishes each occupied half of the space. This represents the opposition, complementary and balance conditions are existed at the same time and space. In Tai Chi Chuan, a posture is a static movement. A good posture has empty and full components, front and back separation, and left and right movement, the physical interpretations related to Yin and Yang Theory. Lao Tzu wrote in his book Dao De Jing "Dao bear one, one bear two and three bear ten thousand things." The Dao he was spoken of is referred to the Wu Chi condition. One is referred to Tai Chi condition. Two is referred to Two Elements condition or Yin and Yang components. One has the potential to become two. This is why it is so wonderful. Two is control by one because two is possible only when one is at the dynamic condition. Therefore, one is capable to transform. When Tai Chi is in the static condition, it returns to Wu Chi condition. A condition that capability to manifest many possibilities. When Tai Chi is in the dynamic condition, it advances to the two elements of Yin and Yang components. Therefore, it is able to divide into four components and ten thousand things later. The multiplication is the following. They are the Yin component and its opposition and the Yang component and its opposition. Each component is interacted to each other so everything is continued to multiple and divided. This is the philosophy of three bear ten thousand things. When ten thousand things multiple, there is development, transformation and death. Chinese martial art is alive because it is transforming based on each practitioner’s contribution and mandate by the physiologic body to transforming naturally. The transformation is based on each practitioner has its distinctive characteristic, personality and it is based on these distinctive characteristic and personality to conduct unpredictable behavior. This transformation is similar to the wavy line in the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol. It has a dynamic spiral transformation to showed innovation, not in a straight line transformation that has no innovation. In Tai Chi Chuan, this wavy line transformation is interpreted as substantial and insubstantial are happened slowly in circular motion in clockwise and counter clockwise directions. It also inspired for a unique approach of Tai Chi Chuan training and confrontational engagement. It is to achieve the best result from the opposite direction. We often observed the following principles applying in Tai Chi Chuan practice which is often referred to as reverse-order training: To approach the left, start from the right; to approach the top, start from the bottom; to accumulate power; start with release; to advance, start with retreat, yielding before discharging, etc. This is the result of when Tai Chi is in the dynamic spiral transformation condition. However, when Tai Chi is in the static spiral transformation condition, it will return to the Wu Chi condition, a condition of mixture of content without any manifestation.

V. Conclusion

Tai Chi Chuan involves physical and spiritual practices. In this complex discipline, it is generally divided into three training levels: they are the physical practice, mind intention and spiritual practice. In the physical practice level, the emphasis is on the execution of each physical movement and the different components and quality involve with the movement, they came from Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol’s features. People often called this symbol the Tai Chi Symbol due to its contribution to Tai Chi Chuan’s principles and practice. In the second mind intention level, the emphasis is on mental creativity relating to Tai Chi Chuan practice and the third level of spiritual practice is on the qi (energy) behind in each movement. The requirements and practice for the last two levels came from Tai Chi Symbol. However, since most of the people practice Tai Chi Chuan is at the physical level. They do not know there is a Tai Chi Symbol or mistaken the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol as Tai Chi Symbol. Therefore, there are many people complained that Tai Chi Chuan is popular today but the quality is poor and there is nobody exactly suggest how to go about to improve the quality of Tai Chi Chuan.

The Tai Chi Symbol gave us the following information. When the universe is transformed from Wu Chi to Tai Chi, the universe is transformed from a condition of chaos to a condition of visible order in which everything is manifested and created. When the Yin and Yang (heaven and earth) visible-entity universe is transformed back to Wu Chi condition, material things cease to exist. Tai Chi is sitting in the middle between the extreme inactive Wu Chi condition and the extreme active Yin and Yang condition. It is known by some practitioners as the opportunity crossroads. Therefore, when Tai Chi moves, it has the ability to move in an active direction as well as in the direction of inactivity. This phenomenon is called opportunity crossroads. One can see, the concept of Tai Chi included energy for transformation and mental creativity for choice.

The formation of the art of Tai Chi Chuan came from several sources. The Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol provided Tai Chi Chuan with philosophical guidance. It is the most important resource for Tai Chi Chuan skill development. It is like a skyscraper built due to the strong foundation. Confucius said “Ten thousand miles begin with the first step.” Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol and Tai Chi Chuan are inseparable. The better one understood the philosophy hidden in this ancient symbol, the better one executes the Tai Chi Chuan movements. The better the skill will be developed.
