articles.title: Interpreting Yin and Yang Theory in Tai Chi Chuan
articles.summary: Studying Tai Chi Chuan properly cannot separate from its many theories. Its theories are very close tight to ancient Chinese philosophy.
articles.content:
1. Introduction

Studying Tai Chi Chuan properly cannot separate from its many theories. Its theories are very close tight to ancient Chinese philosophy. It is only after one has mastered these theories than one’s Tai Chi Chuan skill will have true progress. The function of theory is equivalent to the keys’ function to the house. Among the many theories, Yin and Yang Theory is the key to Tai Chi Chuan training. Therefore, Tai Chi Chuan practitioner should spend his/her time to study this theory well.

Everything that we know of today has its rules of existence and development. It is up to us to uncover these rules, to apply and to follow. One of the features of Tai Chi Chuan training is the unique combination of internal and external substances. Internal and external substances are the same as Yin and Yang components. Therefore, if one does not fully understand the theory of Yin and Yang, it is difficult to have any progress. I think it is necessary for one to clarify this Yin and Yang Theory so one can progress in his/her Tai Chi Chuan training.

2. What is Yin and Yang?

The philosophy of Yin and Yang Theory originally demonstrated in the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol. It is but a simple circle divided into two components known as Yin and Yang components. The circle is referred to as Tai Chi or universe. The black and white components are the Yin and Yang components and some people called this the Yin and Yang Fishes. The black component has a white dot, this mean there is a Yang feature inside the Yin component. The white component has a black dot, this mean there is a Yin feature inside the Yang component. This is to demonstrate that it is the nature of everything that there are opposites and complementary things (forces). When things developed into maturity, they will be transformed. The separation line of the two components is in the shape of an S. This demonstrated the Yin and Yang components’ transformation will be happened slowly and not in smooth order from and into each other. The symbol also indicated that all the transformations are happened as the same time and same space.

Yin and Yang Theory is an ancient Chinese philosophy. It is a study of complementary and opposite forces that exist in the universe. Although the universe is very mysterious, ancient Chinese interpreted everything that exists in the universe can be recognized by divided it into two categories of Yin and Yang components. The sky is Yang and the earth is Yin. Day is Yang and night is Yin. Hot is Yang and cold is Yin. Male is Yang and female is Yin. External is Yang and internal is Yin. Hard power is yang and soft power is Yin. Top is Yang and bottom is Yin. Front is Yang and back is Yin. Advance is Yang and retreat is Yin. Right is Yang and left is Yin. Full is Yang and empty is Yin. People is Yang and the universe is Yin and on down the line. The classification of Yin and Yang components is not absolute. Under certain conditions, a Yin component becomes a Yang component and vice versa. Therefore, everything in the universe can be classified as Yin and Yang components, and Yin and Yang components themselves can continue to be divided into Yin and Yang components in an infinite process. This phenomenon and the characteristics of Yin and Yang components in nature exist everywhere and everything.

A. The Root of Complementary

The Yin and Yang components complementary concept means that when there is no Yin, there will be no Yang. If there is no Yang, there will be no Yin. Yin came from Yang and Yang came from Yin. Yin or Yang by itself does not survive.

B. The Root of Opposites

The Yin and Yang components are opposite concept means that these two components are opposite of each other and they will constantly struggle or position themselves to be on the upper end. This is the basic nature of all things in motion.

C. The Root of Balance

The Yin and Yang components balance concept means that because the two components are constantly positioning themselves to be on the upper end, there will be a temporary balance. This temporary balance is the result of Yin and Yang components are controlling each other.

3. Yin and Yang in Tai Chi Chuan

The Tai Chi Chuan Classics said that the philosophy of Tai Chi came from Wu Chi. When it is in an active form, it is divided into two (Yin and Yang). When it is in an inactive form, it comes together (Wu Chi). From the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol, we see that Tai Chi Chuan is an active form. It is the basic fuel source for all change in the universe. Yin and Yang interaction is the basic rule and motivation of this universal transformation. Since Tai Chi Chuan is an active form, to study it well, one should know the feature of Yin and Yang and their following Yin and Yang relationships and incorporate them into Tai Chi Chuan practices.

A. Yin and Yang Corresponding

It is from this relationship that one understands that if one is working on the left, it is followed by the right; top is followed by the bottom; and front is followed by the back; and so on.

B. Yin and Yang Inclusive

It is from this relationship that one understands that hard contains soft, opening contains closing, defense contains offense, and so on.

C. Yin and Yang Rooting

It is from this relationship that one understands that in order to move the insubstantial foot, one should have already shifted the weight onto the substantial foot, and so on.

D. Yin and Yang as a Complete Unit

It is from this relationship that one understands body integration. When one part moves, the entire body moves. When one part stops, the entire body stops. When the waist does not move, the hands should not move, and so on.

E. Orderly Yin and Yang Interaction

This information reveals that Yin and Yang components are continually changing in a controlled manner, which follows a specific order and rules of change. A movement begins on the left foot than continues onto the right foot. When the feet finish, the movement continues with the hands.

F. Progressive Yin and Yang Transformation

This information reveals that Yin and Yang transformation has several options. Generally, this transformation happens in the following fashion: slowly in a spiral motion. When executing a movement, one should incorporate the waist rotation to lead the four limbs to move in order to achieve body integration. Therefore, this transformation has quantity and quality differences.

G. Unpredictable Yin and Yang Transformation

Although we know that Yin and Yang components are constantly changing, the rate of change we do not know, so the result is unknown. Since the result is unknown, it is unpredictable. In Tai Chi Chuan practice, due to the fact that most of the body’s weight is supported by one leg, one is capable of changing direction to head into any direction one wants. Therefore, Tai Chi Chuan is very mobile. Mobility is the essence of martial art. Therefore, there are people called mobility is the soul of martial art.

From the Yin and Yang relationships described from above, we should expect to see that Yin and Yang components are existed everywhere in the Tai Chi Chuan solo form. The Yin and Yang components in Tai Chi Chuan are interpreted as the followings in the solo form practice. It is the hard and soft powers. It is the fast and slow movements. It is the extension and contraction of the muscle groups. It is the coordination of top and bottom body. It is the internal substances and external substances harmony. It is the opening and closing motion. It is the empty and full body weight. It is the advancing and retreating steps. It is the left and right motions of the eyes. It is the active and inactive of the mind, etc. Following is a brief description of some of the Yin and Yang components and how they are related to solo form practice.

a. Empty and Full Distinguishable

It is very important in Tai Chi Chuan practice to be able to understand the empty and full concept. The Tai Chi Chuan Classics pointed out the fault of “Double Weight” due to the locked of the concept of “Empty and Full”. Generally, in Tai Chi Chuan practice, empty refers to the top and full refers to the bottom of the body. Here, top refers to the upper body. The upper body has to be relaxed so that the qi will sink to the dantian (an area three inches below the navel). Therefore, one will feel that the body is very light as if empty. Bottom refers to the lower body. When the feet are full, it forms a strong foundation and supporting. Therefore, empty the top means suspend the head from above, relax the shoulders and sink the elbows, relax the chest and raise the back, loosen the waist and pull the abdomen inward. Full in the bottom means to pull the buttock inward, open the groin, bend the knees and point the toes forward. The bottom has to be full in order to be stable. The top has to be empty so that it will be easy to move. This empty and full concept apply everywhere throughout the body in Tai Chi Chuan practice. It can apply solely on the feet, hands, and at a combative situation. After one understands this concept, the body is better to perform balance, coordination and mobility.

b. Hard and Soft Practices

Tai Chi Chuan appears to be soft because one only sees the relaxation, soft and slow motion and not the tension, hard and fast motion in the Tai Chi Chuan solo form practice. This leads many people to believe that this is how Tai Chi Chuan works. In Tai Chi Chuan practice, relax, empty and soft are close relatives. Tension, fullness and hardness are also close relatives. They are very similar and yet there is something that keeps them apart. Relaxation and tension are internal fundamental principles. Empty and full function based on this fundamental principle. Hard and soft is the external expression of relaxation and tension, and empty and full. This hard and soft concept should not be understood as “hardness” like rock and “softness” like water, rather, one should understand it as the result of physiologic relaxation or one should understand it in relationship to flesh and bone of the human body as “firm”. Therefore, one should understand hard as firm, a condition of alert, stableness, lightness and nimbleness. It is a result of total body relaxation and coordination. This is why many instructors ask their students to perform Tai Chi Chuan in a relaxed, soft and slow way. The truth is that when there is lightness, there is balance. When there is softness, there much has hardness. If there is no concentration and balance, there can not be lightness, nimbleness and mobility.

c. Fast and Slow Movements

Tai Chi Chuan is one of the internal Chinese martial art styles. As in all martial arts, the movements have to be executed quickly in order to be effective. However, people observe Tai Chi Chuan movements are done slowly for the following reasons:

1. To obtain total body relaxation

2. To master the circular motion

3. To concentrate on all the Yin and Yang components.

4. Self-examination of all the movements

5. To develop continuity

6. To maintain normal breathing pattern

7. To maintain internal communication:

a. Internal organs’ movement and proper functioning

b. Harmonize the nervous system

c. Acknowledge the qi circulation

8. Eliminate waste of excess energy

9. Emphasis the important of body movement over four limbs

10. To better understand how the principles are applied to the movements

11. It is better to work on the Tai Chi Chuan fundamentals

12. Presenting Tai Chi Chuan as a performing art

Fast is not referring to the speed of executing each movement in Tai Chi Chuan. Rather, it is referring to the transition of each movement. When one is properly fine tune the body from the 12 points described from above, one will be able to execute each movement with swift and ease. Swift and ease are the objective and slowness is the training method to get there. Therefore, slow and fast are some of Tai Chi Chuan’s characteristics. When the movement is done slow, it does not mean the slower the better as some people suggested. Speed is based on one’s ability to execute the 12 points described above. If one is in good physical condition, obviously, one can practice the movements more quickly than those who are not in the same physical condition.

d. Opening and Closing Motions

In Tai Chi Chuan, every movement has an opening and closing motions. Opening is expanding from inside to outside. Closing is contracting from outside to inside. Therefore, opening and closing are also known as extension and contraction. Tai Chi Chuan practice is the worked on the motions of opening and closing and vice versa leaded by the spine. When it is an opening, it is large and expansive and there is no more space outside. When it is a closing, it is so compact and tight that there is no more space inside. For a beginner, the opening motion should be bigger so that there is more stretching on the muscles, ligaments and tendons so the qi and power will be reached to the body’s extremities. For an experienced practitioner, the opening motion will be smaller to work on many different types of muscle groups. From the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol, we understood that Yin and Yang are capable to have infinite process of division. Therefore, among each opening and closing motions, there is subdivision into smaller opening and closing motions to better work on qi circulation inside the entire body. This was what Yang Cheng Fu (1883-1936) meant when he said “First, one should practice the extension form and later the compact form.”

e. Top and Bottom, Left and Right, Front and Back

The definition of this three pairs: top and bottom, left and right, and front and back, is very common and easy to understand. Each movement must take care of the opposite side. When one is working on the left side, one must be aware of the right side. When one is doing the top, one must be aware of the bottom. When one is working on the front, one must be aware of the back. There should be a coordination of the opposite so that the body will move as a unit, each part should be corresponded and communicated with one another to attain body integration. Otherwise, the activity will be harmful to one’s body.

f. Relaxation and Tension

Relaxation is the most basic in Tai Chi Chuan practice. It requires the whole body to relax during activity. From the brain, the nervous system, muscles groups, ligaments, tendons, joints, connective tissues and organs. When the body is relaxed, soft and flexible, the mind is calm, clear and focused. One is able to perform fluidity motion. The Yin and Yang Theory explains that one can not survive without the opposite. Therefore, all the movements should be relaxed, firm and have structure. Although the Tai Chi Chuan practitioners do not talk about the tension as we know it, tension in Tai Chi Chuan is defined as the pressure one felt from twisting and stretching of the body, arms and legs. From this tension and relaxation or twisting and releasing, extra exercise goes to the body’s joints, muscles, the nervous system and internal organs as suggested in the Yin and Yang Theory. Relaxation and tension support each other. The more one relaxes, the more one is able to maintain tense or twist and stretch. The more one is able to stretch and twist, the more one is able to relax. This process is equivalent to produce fine steel. This is why the body is nimble and the mind is clear, calm and concentrated. Throughout the Tai Chi Chuan solo form, we often see the upper body is relaxed and the lower body is filled with tension to support the body. When the hands close into a powerful fist, the muscles on the shoulders and elbows remain relax so the power is confined at the fist. One can see, relaxation in Tai Chi Chuan practice is but based on how to manage the relationship between tension and relaxation. Today, most of the people who practice Tai Chi Chuan emphasized more on relaxation than tension because tension occur more in life. When we are excited about something or when we step into a new environment, our body automatically tenses. Practicing Tai Chi Chuan regularly can recognize and remove this tension. A new product developed called firm. Due to the function of Tai Chi Chuan practice is able to reduce tension, it is popular as a form of stress management technique today by many practitioners. It is a perfect medicine for today’s stressful society.

g. Active and Inactive

In Tai Chi Chuan, tranquility attain from actively involvement with the Tai Chi Chuan solo form practice. This is different from most people understood tranquility as no physical movement. The Tai Chi Chuan Classics written that a practitioner should look for tranquility in action or tranquility during physical activity. Seeking tranquility from activity is a Yin and Yang concepts of excitation and depression. We know that absolute depression and absolute tranquility do not exist.

Applying the consciousness to quiet the excitation is a very difficult task, especially since we are living in a society where temptations exist everywhere. This is why in ancient China, Daoists lived in isolation to remove themselves from temptations. The more one is consciously to remove these temptations and though, the more they appear. Therefore, confronting them directly is the best method to manage them. It is the true tranquility. Tai Chi Chuan practice is but one of many technical methods to manage them by attempting to achieve the internal condition of tranquility as the result of external behavior. This is achieved for the practitioner by focusing on one behavior or stimulant and screen out all others. Therefore, in order to develop a mental tranquility by practice the physical Tai Chi Chuan solo form movements, the movements should be lightness, relax, softness and smooth. It is providing a better serenity environment to practice to have good outcome.

h. Inside and Outside Substances

The Tai Chi Chuan solo form is the physical interpretation of Tai Chi philosophy in Tai Chi Chuan practice. Inside contribution is referred to the function of the mind intention which governed by the internal three harmonies. Outside contribution is referred to the function of body movement which governed by the external three harmonies. When the body relaxes, it will be calm and refine the nervous system function. When the nervous system is relaxed, it is better regulate, coordinate and communicate better with the body’s organs and their functions so that the whole body can be relaxed and in a better conditon. This is what Yang Cheng Fu means in the Ten Important Points when he said that inside much be coordinated with outside in order to attain in Tai Chi Chuan skill.

Now, we see that Yin and Yang components do not refer to one thing. It simply refers to things that exist in duality. Although in our society, Yin and Yang components are recognized as opposite of each other, this is but a tool to differentiate one’s existence. We must recognize the three concpets of complementary, balance and opposition in the same space and time. From this Yin and Yang components interaction and transformation, many things can and will be manifested. In order to for one to advance in Tai Chi Chuan skill, one must understand the Yin and Yang definitions and relationship as described above and applying them to Tai Chi Chuan practice accordingly. This is why the Tai Chi Chuan Classics say that whenever one correctly applied the Yin and Yang components in action is the criterion for determining one’s Tai Chi Chuan skills. Today, there are many people practice the Tai Chi Chuan solo form either too hard or too soft.

i. Stretching in the Opposite Direction

One of the objectives for bodily stretching is to developing the warding-off jin power in Tai Chi Chuan practice. All Chinese martial art styles developed specific exercises to improve bodily condition. In Tai Chi Chuan, ward-off jin power developed from stretching the body. Without this jin power, Tai Chi Chuan cannot function as a martial art. In order to develop this jin power, Every part of the body involves with a movement should be stretching to improve their conditions. Generally, people are not born physically prepare for martial art’s vigorous physical activity. Therefore, all Chinese martial art styles developed exercises to improve body condition. These types of exercise are commonly called gong-exercises. For example, in Tai Chi Chuan, the head is suspending from above, sinking the shoulders, pointing the elbows, opening the pelvic and bending the knees, etc. These requirements imply to stretch the body. During Tai Chi Chuan practice, any movement one is making be aware of the bodily stretching requirement.

4. The Common Mistakes One Made from not Understanding the Yin and Yang Theory

There are two most common mistakes one made from not understand Yin and Yang Theory. They are double weight and not differentiate substantial from insubstantial.

A. Double Weight

Double weight is the term written by Wang Tsung Yueh (1525-1606) in his Tai Chi Chuan Treatise. He said “People spend decade practice Tai Chi Chuan still control by other. It is because one does not understand Yin and Yang.” This double weight has three common meaning today. It is referred to both feet have the equal amount weight of supporting the body’s. The second meaning is referred to the same side of the hand and foot from the body has the power. The third meaning often associate with Tai Chi Chuan practitioners and that is that when one is engaged the opponent, one should apply the tactical strategy of given up on oneself and follow the opponent’s action principle. For most of the Chinese martial art styles, they are highly recommended confrontational strategy. When the opponent applies to strike, one confronts the strike with power as well.

B. Substantial and Insubstantial Not Differentiate

Differentiate substantial and insubstantial is one of Ten Essential Points for Tai Chi Chuan practice recommended by Yang Cheng Fu. If one is not able to have substantial and insubstantial differentiated it is difficult to have mobility and agility. They are the soul of martial art’s random and spontaneous actions and reactions. Mobility and agility are the nature of martial art.

5. Yin and Yang in Martial Art Application

In Chinese martial art, it does not matter whether the technique is for offense or defense purpose. It cannot be separated from Yin and Yang transformation. In martial art activity, simple movements such as stepping forward or backward, ascending or descending, opening or closing, extending or contracting, all are involved in Yin and Yang transformation. Yin and Yang transformation is the source of Tai Chi Chuan’s technical application manifestation. Thus, Yin and Yang Theory contains the secret of Chinese martial art.

In the Yin and Yang Theory, the information about Yin and Yang complementary and opposition components exists within the same space and time. Yin and Yang does not refer to specific things. They are names, not shapes. Generally, when something is outside, visible, active, advancing, ascending, hot and strong power, etc., it is referred to as a Yang component. When something is inside, invisible, inactive, retreating, descending, cold and soft power, etc., it is referred to as a Yin component.

Chinese martial art engagement training and strategy were developed based on the Yin and Yang philosophy from the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol. This symbol shows us that Yin and Yang components is presenting and functioning in the same space at the same time. Their activities and interactions have the following tactics, relationships and outcomes: Yang then Yin, Yin then Yang, Yin and Yang together, Yin and Yang present, Yin and Yang interaction, and Yin turns into Yang or Yang turns into Yin.

A. Yang then Yin

Yang then Yin tactics and relationships means first strong then weak. This phenomenon often leads to confrontation and collision.

B. Yin then Yang

Yin then Yang tactics and relationship means first yield then follow up with a strike. There is a time difference.

C. Yin and Yang Together

If Yin and Yang exist together as separate entities, the situation is not possible. If Yin and Yang are together as two components of the same unit, the situation is good.

D. Yin and Yang Present

In this Yin and Yang present tactics and relationship, Yin and Yang exist together at the same time in the same space. This is very good.

E. Yin and Yang Interaction

This Yin and Yang interaction tactics and relationship is similar to the philosophy of Tai Chi. The prerequisite in this relationship is Yin and Yang components capable of functioning independently. It is best when there are Yin and Yang together and Yin and Yang present.

F. Yin Turns into Yang or Yang Turns into Yin

In this Yin turns into Yang or Yang turns into Yin tactics and relationship, Yin is intercepting all actions then following up with Yang action. When one has more time with Yin, the greater the outcome from Yang, vice versa.

6. Yin and Yang Balance is a Sign of Advancement

Chinese martial art has a long history, since the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644 ), it is divided into internal martial art and external martial art systems, has many styles, has three major technical trainings in forms (bare hands and weapons), gong-exercises (dynamic and static conditions) and combat stimulations (solo drill and partner drills), six major techniques in kicking, punching, fist striking, palm striking, grappling and wrestling and it has multiple functions as combat art, performing art, nurturing life art, health maintenance exercise and personal development, etc. In another words, Chinese martial art has vast body of information. However, the basic feature of this vast body of information is about physical activity. The basic requirement in any physical activity is about body balance. The quality of body balance is determined the quality of the physical activity. Since martial art is one of the physical activities, the quality of body balance yields quality martial art skill. The first and most important function as a martial art is its combat function. As a combat art, power and technique are the decisive elements to victory. Therefore, if one is able to coordinate the muscle groups to work together, executing the techniques will be smooth, swift, versatility and discharging the power will be powerful to cause a lot of devastation. Therefore, in martial art training, one should understand the significant value of body balance. Without quality body balance, one cannot perform any quality physical movement, prompt deliver an effective and powerful strike. If one locks of this body balance ability, one cannot talk about physical activity and martial art. Today, there are many physical activities and performances ignored the value of body balance and not able to attained good result. However, Chinese martial art recognized the significant of this body balance contribution and introduced zhan zhuang (standing meditation) exercise training, solo form practice and push-hands exercise as some of the fundamentals trainings to improve the body balance. Therefore, we see among Chinese martial art styles, zhan zhuang exercise training is introduced as the first lesson in Chinese martial art training to the students.

Tai Chi Chuan as in all Chinese martial art styles, it is highly emphasized on body balance. Body balance has physical and mental balance. Yin and Yang balance is a higher form of balance. This is the balance Chinese martial art attempts to accomplish by offering three types of trainings in martial art forms, combat simulations and gong-exercises. In order to better understand balance, one should understand the following four basic terms.

A. Body balance

The body is generally had static balance in its nature state. The body or any object affected by the external force can cause it to move. However, maintaining the body balance is its natural ability. It does not matter something is in the micro or macro world, everything in its natural state is balance.

B. Center of gravity

The weight of an object is the combination of the weights of many bodily parts and function points. Different part of the body has its own center of gravity. Therefore, the center gravity of the body is the combination of many different bodily parts put together. This center gravity of the body is changing according to the blood circulation, breathing and body positioning. The center gravity is located inside the body as well as outside the body. It is depended on how the body is positioned.

C. Localize balance

It is referred to the condition from different bodily parts after activity performed. For example, muscular contraction and extension on the hands

D. Entire body balance

It is referred to the balance of an entire object. In order to have the entire body balance, one has to neutralize all the external forces from outside the body to maintain balance. Generally, it has three conditions.

i. Adjusting balance

It does not matter how the body is positioning due to the external force. The body does not move up and down. It maintains in the same position.

ii. Stable balance

Although the object moved after the external force applied, it maintains by returning to the same position after the external force stop.

iii. No balance

When the external force is applying to an object, it moved and it could not return to its original position.

E. Yin and Yang Components Balance

Although Tai Chi Chuan push-hands exercise has many pre-programmed operations, they are but teach the students how to maintain body balance and re-balance under certain competition situation and then maneuver the body and its parts for offense and defense in martial art confrontational engagement. The nature of martial art confrontational engagement is that all actions are spontaneous. The pre-programmed operational exercises are but tangible method to teach the spontaneous actions, reactions and outcomes. There are many methods to practice this. Push-hands exercise is but a Chinese martial art combat simulation training method introduced in Tai Chi Chuan style. There are some people recommended to directly work on the spontaneous outcome by focusing on Yin and Yang components application. We knew that Yin and Yang Theory offering four types of information. They are opposition, complementary, balance and interaction. Since the nature of Yin and Yang components balance is not a constant condition and Yin and Yang components interaction is not an invincible condition in martial art engagement, push-hands exercise is but a matter of how well one applies the Yin and Yang components to match the opponent’s Yin and Yang components. It is a subject of one applies Yin or Yang component to disrupt the opponent’s Yin or Yang component to cause the opponent’s body to off-balance. It is very scientific. It is the subject involves with body balance, center of gravity, localize balance and entire body balance, etc.

Yin and Yang balance has many levels based on its quality. The highest balance is harmony. Balance is the beginning and ending of all things. The Tai Chi Chuan Classics written that Yin and Yang interaction is called dongjin skill. It is only when one has dongjin skill. One has Tai Chi Chuan martial skill. It developed from Tai Chi Chuan push-hands exercise. Xu Yu Sheng (1878-1945) had said that if one engages in Tai Chi Chuan training without push-hands exercise training, it had no value in martial art skill.

The Yellow Empire’s Internal Medicine Classic pointed out that if one is attended and refined all the Yin and Yang components in the body. One will achieve better health because the Yin and Yang components are better balance. Balancing the body’s Yin and Yang components is also the basic requirement and condition for successful martial art training and skill development. A quality Yin and Yang components balance determine the quality of the body condition and capability. The objective of the different martial art training methods is to attain Yin and Yang components balance. The different in many methods is due to the different in styles. Although there are three major methods of Chinese martial art training (forms, combat simulations and gong-exercises), the objective is the same. It is to find the best solution to solve the relationship between Yin and Yang component in balance so that one is able to achieve the best body balance possible. It is only when one has body balance than one is capable to launch a powerful strike. We know that any behavior is the result of mental activity. Therefore, it is only when one has mental balance than attain physical balance is possible. The training methods, their qualities and effective results are but serve as the tools to accomplish the best balance between Yin and Yang components which divided into many levels. Today, there are many different exercises available. They are the results of many forebears’ researched and experienced. It does not matter in the macro-world or micro-world, everything in its natural state is balance. When it influenced or interrupted by the external force, this natural balance state had been broken and it is necessary to establish a new balance. Otherwise, one will get sick and everything is in chaos. Let’s take for an example that we are facing daily. When an infant was born, his/her body is in a balance state so the muscular structure in the body during activity is not so obvious divided into extension and relaxation. However, as this new infant grows older, the muscles groups in the body are developed into vary degree of extension and relaxation during activity. By lifting weight or picking up things, the muscle structures in the hands will be developed into extension and contraction motions, etc., every time when he moves. Therefore, the natural balance state had been broken and it is necessary to establish a new balance to survive onto a new life style and habit. This balancing process, due to the necessary to survive from the new environment, will continue to adjust to come up with a newer balance. This re-adjustment process for stable balance is nonstop for a person from infant to his/her senior. For this reason, there are some people who are able to continue to re-adjusting to this new balance to keep the body healthy. On the other hand, there are people who are not able to regularly re-adjusting the body to maintain balance, these people will quickly and easily get sick.

7. Conclusion

The Tai Chi Chuan’s 13 postures of warding off, roll back, press, push, pull down, split, shoulder strike, elbow strike, looking to the left, looking to the right, step forward, step backward and body equilibriums are but the basic building block of Tai Chi Chuan. If one spends the time to practice and to understand, soon or later, one will understand the role of Yin and Yang components is the source of information for Tai Chi Chuan’s 13 postures. One will understand the significant of Yin and Yang components’ present, motion and interaction in Tai Chi Chuan, his/her Tai Chi Chuan skill is beginning to make progress. It is only after one understood the meaning of Yin and Yang Theory, applied, incorporated and evaluated are based on the Yin and Yang Theory to one’s training and practice. One will have dongjin skill in Tai Chi Chuan. The more one practices, the better the skill one will be able to attain. One has truly mastered the training method to attain wisdom.

articles.title: The Three Emphases as an Internal Martial Art
articles.summary: Chinese martial art has a long history and it is one of the great cultural traditions of China. Countless innovations, improvements and developments have yielded the various styles, solo forms, partner forms, weapon forms and training methods of today.
articles.content:
I. Introduction

Chinese martial art has a long history and it is one of the great cultural traditions of China. Countless innovations, improvements and developments have yielded the various styles, solo forms, partner forms, weapon forms and training methods of today. Emphasizing internal and external practices, its benefits include health maintenance and body conditioning and it provides a self-defense method, a competitive sport, a performance art, and general entertainment. Moreover, the exercise refines the heart and soul.

Although the Chinese martial art share many characteristics and techniques such as kicking, hitting, wresting, grappling, striking and stabbing, and the body turns, twists, bends, balances, jumps and falls, they have developed into many distinctive styles and varieties with specific objectives. The most common distinction is the internal and external systems.

The terminology of internal and external martial art was first applied by Huang Zong Yi (1610-1695), a historian who lived at the end of the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) and the beginning of the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911). In the document Wang Zheng Man Mu Zhi Ming (The Inscription on Wang Zheng Man’s tombstone), Huang wrote “Shaolin was famous with the fist. It emphasizes controlling others. It has flaws. There is also the existence of the internal art. It applies the strategy of static to control the dynamic. As soon as contact is made, an opponent falls down. It differs from Shaolin. This art begins with Zheng San Feng. Zheng San Feng was a Daoist priest who lived in Wudang Mountain.”

II. The Three Emphases

Chinese martial art has developed into many styles today. Although determining whether a style is belonging to the internal or external type was a controversial issue throughout history, generally, both show differences in the following three areas: name, features and training methods.

A. Name

To understand the meaning of internal and external styles of Chinese martial art, one should begin with the understanding and the formation of the vocabularies. There are many reasons behind the names. I list two here.

1. The first definition is based on philosophical studies. External refers to outside the family and internal refers to inside the family. There are three major philosophical teachings in China: Buddhism, Confucianism and Daoism. People who study Buddhism, such as monks, generally study in a monastery, not at home, and cannot marry to have a family. Therefore, they are considered living outside the family. During the developmental stages of Daoism, people who studied it, such as Daoist priests, generally studied at home and could marry to have a family. Therefore, they were considered living inside the family. The martial art took the monks practice as referring to the external styles, and took the practice of the Daoist priests as referring to the internal styles.

2. The second definition is based on a common statement. “Internally, one trains the qi. Externally, one trains the sinews, ligaments bones and skins.” Therefore, when one’s training emphasizes the qi, it is called internal, and when one’s training emphasizes the sinews, ligaments, bones and skins, it is called external. A powerful and effective martial strike is based on the coordination of the two. Therefore, when a style places more emphasis on the qi than the sinews, ligaments, bones and skins, it is an internal style of Chinese martial art. Favoring the training of sinews, bones and skin are the external Chinese martial art.

B. Features

Chinese martial art appears to have many features, but a closer inspection reveals four in common. They are the application of power, the strategy involved, the technique involved and the type of practitioner.

1. Pre-heaven power and post-heaven power

The pre-heaven power, also known as inborn power or natural power, is the power generated from muscle contraction. The post-heaven power, also known as internal power and integrated power, is the power generated from the coordination of the entire body. External styles often apply the pre-heaven power to strike. Internal styles often apply the post-heaven power to strike.

2. Strike first and strike second

Strike first is initiating one’s own action. It is the strategy often employing by the external style practitioners. Strike second is the reaction based on the opponent’s action. It is the strategy often employing by the internal style practitioners.

3. Technique and power

External styles highly emphasize the technical applications and variations behind each technique. Internal styles highly emphasize the power behind each technique. Therefore, the same technique employed by both internal and external style practitioners yielded different results.

4. Physical appearance

External style practitioners generally look much more muscular than the internal style practitioners.

C. Training methods

An effective technique generally involves accuracy, speed and power. The major difference between the internal and external styles involves the delivery of power. Therefore, the primary difference in training involves power training, and the secondary difference is body manipulation. Power training refers to such things as stretching the ligaments and tendons and body manipulation refers to all the bodily motions. Since Tai Chi Chuan is an internal Chinese martial art style, it is different from most of the Chinese martial art systems and styles. And every usage and practice in Tai Chi Chuan differs from our daily activities. Therefore, one should not compare Tai Chi Chuan practices to a typical habit. External Chinese martial art styles and sports use power in their performance. Generally, one can see the differences of Tai Chi Chuan training from other Chinese martial art styles in three areas. 1) The training emphasizes following principles, not physical power like most Chinese martial art styles. 2) The training emphasizes improving the root, not the function, like many health maintenance exercises do today. 3) The training emphasizes improving the body condition and composition, unlike most martial art styles, which focus on the application of individual techniques.

1. The training emphasizes principles, not power

Here, principle refers to Tai Chi philosophy. Zheng San Feng created Tai Chi Chuan based on Daoist philosophy and Lao Tzu’s teachings. Therefore, to study Tai Chi Chuan correctly, one should understand the philosophy from the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol, or Yin and Yang Theory, some of Daoism’s canonical works, traditional Chinese medical theory, and The Internal Classic of the Yellow Emperor.

In order to better understand Tai Chi Chuan and practice it correctly, one must

understand the philosophy from the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol, or Yin and Yang theory. The Tai Chi Chuan Treatise written by Wang Tsung Yueh (1525-1606) said, “Tai Chi came from Wu Chi, the mother of Yin Yang.” Lao Tzu's Dao De Jing says, “Tai Chi is born from One, One gave birth to two, two gave birth to three, three gave birth to ten thousand things.” “Dao” is also known as “Wu Chi” or “Void.” “One” refers to “Wu Chi”. It is also referred to as “Great Void”. This “Great Void” refers to emptiness that is filled with qi, or energy. It is the original source of a body’s health condition. “Two” refers to the Yin and Yang components. The Tai Chi Chuan Classics written, “The heaven and earth are one great Tai Chi. The human body is one small Tai Chi.” One can see that “two” is manifested in Tai Chi Chuan movements as substantial and insubstantial, hard and soft, fast and slow, opening and closing, round and square, and so on. “Three” refers to three dimensions. One sees this manifested as circular motion or spiral motion in Tai Chi Chuan movements. Therefore, “Great Void” is the true nature of Tai Chi and its manifestation of relaxation, softness, lightness, and agility.

The requirements of Tai Chi Chuan practice are: “Applying the mind, not physical power”; “Applying the mind intention to guide the qi”; “Applying the qi to circulate throughout the body.” The meaning behind these statements is to have a relaxed, tranquil, and natural body. When the body is natural, tranquil and relaxed, it is easier for the conscious spirit to appear and function. The concept of “relaxation” in Tai Chi Chuan is the external expression of the Yin component. It is equivalent to the concept of “empty and insubstantial” in Daoist philosophy. If the body is relaxed, the qi circulates better inside the body. This is as if the body were empty, there is room for more invisible qi. The more qi the body has, the greater its strength and the better its material composition. The mind and body relaxation requirements are indirectly guided by one’s conscious spirit to function better in the processes of mobilizing the body’s qi, circulating the blood, and clearing the body’s meridian channels to cultivate the original qi. “Tranquility” is associated with the quality of calmness. Generally, when there is calmness, the conscious spirit appears. This is often expressed as “applying the tranquility to nurture the spirit.” The substance called qi does not occupy any space, nor does it have mass or shape. It is an intangible substance. In order to improve this substance, one should work with something that shares the feature of intangibility, such as a principle.

2. The training emphasizes the root, not the function

What is the root of Tai Chi Chuan? It is the original substance that fuels every living thing. As the Daoist literature states, “You can say a thousand words to explain it. It is but to clear the mind, enhanced the root to cultivate the original qi, and strengthen the body condition. This produces a result better than your opponent’s.” The “root” of Tai Chi Chuan is qi and qi cultivation. When the Tai Chi Chuan training emphasizes the root, one is placing emphasis on improving the body condition by increasing the qi inside the body. However, when the Tai Chi Chuan training emphasizes the “function,” one is placing emphasis on the benefit and application of each individual technique. Improving the condition of the qi and the awareness and coordination of the whole body agrees with Tai Chi Chuan's philosophy.

One can see that the training which focuses on the root aims to enhance the foundation as well as the original qi. It yields the best result when it follows the philosophy of having the body’s inside and outside attributes working together. “When one enhances the root, the tree will have many leaves. When one supplements the spring, it will last longer.” When one is strictly practicing and refining each Tai Chi Chuan movement with specific instruction, it is but following the method of “enhanced the root, supplement the spring.” When enhancing the original qi and the kidney qi during Tai Chi Chuan practice by incorporating waist rotation into each movement, the condition of the physiologic organs improves and energizes, and one will have quicker reaction time and better coordination. In addition, enhancing the qi also benefits the upper body with agility, the mid-section with vitality, and the lower body with stability. These are the important ingredients for a powerful martial art strike.

Practicing Tai Chi Chuan correctly means following the instruction of “regulate the spirit, regulate the breathing, and regulate the body.” This instruction is common to qigong discipline. Qigong is a simple exercise to enhance and nurture the root. Therefore, Tai Chi Chuan is also known as a dynamic qigong exercise of the Daoist school. In Tai Chi Chuan, the instruction for the mind intention is to provide specific qi circulation inside the body, so that each movement will agree with Tai Chi Chuan’s requirements, features, and rules. With a conscientious effort to develop the root, Tai Chi Chuan practice can enhance the qi and refine the body.

Through dedication, the quality of Tai Chi Chuan movements is improved. The improved movements are observably better coordinated, and all the movements are initiated from the rotation of the waist. This improvement is the result of incorporating waist rotation into Tai Chi Chuan practice such as the following: dynamic qigong exercise, Tai Chi Chuan solo form practice, solo drill exercise, shaking the spear exercise, and dynamic push hand exercise. These all train the martial fundamentals for more power and coordination, and enhance the original qi. As one can see, Tai Chi Chuan is a complete Chinese martial art style that has a very extensive curriculum.

Regarding balance, the Tai Chi Chuan Treaties written, “When one part of the body moves, all parts of the body follow. When one part is inactive, all parts should be inactive.” “When outside and inside are inactive, applying the inactive to neutralize the active.” Throughout the entire Tai Chi Chuan solo form practice, if one pays attention to all the active and inactive attributes, one will execute each movement in a balanced and comfortable manner.

3. The training emphasizes refining the movements, not learning new movements

Here, refining refers to the body’s movement, the quality of the movement and its components. If a person’s training emphasizes only on the application of individual techniques, he or she will forego Tai Chi Chuan's multiple benefits. This is similar to writing Chinese calligraphy. If one only pays attention to each individual stroke, neglecting the character as a whole, the calligraphy is poorly done.

In some aspects, Tai Chi Chuan is like all martial art styles. Each movement must be proper and powerful, and stepping must be quick. The body, hands and feet have to move quickly with coordination and power. The eyes have to be sharp. In summary, one has to train the body well so that it is very light, balanced and nimble, and the skin is very sensitive so one can easily detect the opponent's movement and power. This requires the body to be in an optimum condition. It is the result of quality training, not quantity training. One observes that Tai Chi Chuan movements are done slowly and powerlessly. This seems counter to all principles of martial art, which imply that each movement has to be done quickly and powerfully. However, there is a common saying among Tai Chi Chuan practitioners, that to practice the solo form slowly is to work on the martial fundamentals, and to practice the solo form quickly is to work on the martial application. The Tai Chi Chuan solo form is done slowly to work on body mechanics and as fundamentals training, so one is able to move quickly when needed.

To demonstrate all the hard and soft attributes in Tai Chi Chuan, externally one should perform the solo form softly, firmly and with agility. Internally, one should perform the solo form with concentration, clearly defining substantial and insubstantial. In other words, when the body has hard and soft attributes, the body is able to act very quickly; yielding and discharging powers seem to happen at the same time. The body’s coordination and balance appear supported from all directions. The muscles’ activities and the physiologic organs are highly coordinated. If the body has an excess of either hard or soft attributes, it cannot act harmoniously. This is why the Tai Chi Chuan Classics prefers 50% from each attribute as the best combination.

The Tai Chi Chuan Treaties says, “The mind controls the qi; let mind calm and sink so the qi can penetrate inside the bone.” “One should concentrate on the spirit, not on qi; if the concentration is on the qi, it causes stagnation.” These quotations indicate that during Tai Chi Chuan practice, what one should follow and concentrate on—in every movement—is based on the mind intention, not power. Let the mind intention move first, then the physical movement follows. If one follows this method the mind intention will get there first, followed by the qi. When the qi gets there, the power will follow. When the movement is calm, stable and has control, it has the potential to yield a lot of power. If one follows this method of practicing Tai Chi Chuan regularly, the qi will penetrate into the bones, and a higher level of qi circulation will prepare the body for more rigorous activity. In addition to the above, one practices Tai Chi Chuan should pay attention to stretching the body and bodily joints to improve the qi circulation, body integration, and the elasticity of muscles, ligaments and tendons. Also, pay attention to the spiral rotation of the waist, upper and lower body coordination, and unifying inside and outside in each movement. After the body is trained, one can see a simple and gentle waving of the hand yielding a lot of power.

Tai Chi Chuan martial skill should be performed based on the opponent’s action. Generally speaking, it should be centered on the opponent’s action and situation. The Tai Chi Chuan Classics says, “When one has attained skill, one engages the opponent instinctually without thinking. When the technique comes, it will come naturally.” Tai Chi Chuan practitioner often said that there is no technique in practice but there is technique in application. This is the result of a well-trained body. Tai Chi Chuan is one of the fine traditions of Chinese culture. It has a long history with an extensive body of knowledge. It is both old and new. It is elegant and simple. It is a martial art and a performing art. It is the product of ancient Chinese philosophy, traditional Chinese medicine, Chinese martial art, natural living art, and health maintenance exercise. From this, one can see that it differs from conventional sports. During Tai Chi Chuan practice, emphasis is placed on: the mind intention directing all the movements, sinking the qi, a tranquil mind and a relaxed body, and natural breathing. In addition, as with all martial art training, it is necessary to have the coordination of the hands, eyes, body and stepping. As such, Tai Chi Chuan is a discipline of bodily integration. Regularly practicing Tai Chi Chuan is good for the body’s central nervous system, circulatory system, respiratory system, muscular skeletal system, and body metabolism.

III. Conclusion

With the recent surge of interest in Tai Chi Chuan as a health exercise, there are many health enthusiasts wondering how its slow, relaxed and soft movements can be applied as a martial art. Wang Tsung Yueh (1525-1606) wrote in the Tai Chi Chuan Treatise that Chinese martial art styles and tactics have many options. Although the techniques differ, most of them represented the strong bullying the weak, the swift defeating the slow. This is the result of natural ability, not of physical science.” And Huang Zhong Yi’s son Huang Bai Jia wrote in The techniques of Internal Art that “The external art of Shaolin had wonderful techniques. Zheng San Feng was excellent at Shaolin. He made some changes, and the result of these changes is called Internal Art.”

From the above two quotations, we can see that the traditional Chinese martial art were but the strong and swift defeating the weak and slow. It was based on one’s naturally ability, until Zheng San Feng came along and changed this. The changes he made emphasized the three areas already mentioned. Achievement was no longer based on one’s natural ability. The emphasis shifted to applying physical science into the art so that every technique was properly executed and power was delivered efficiently. Through emphasizing the fundamentals, one is well prepared to achieve the best outcomes. Through emphasizing internal power by manipulating the body, one develops the qi more than individual application techniques. Yet every strike is powerful. With body manipulation, the qi better permeates the entire body so that each motion has rooting, coordination and power. This alone guarantees that each strike has power.

One can see that the internal martial art style created by Zheng San Feng was developed from the external style of Chinese martial art. This is why people concluded that the internal martial art style was superior. However, it takes more time to reach proficiency because every movement is done opposite from nature habit. Zheng San Feng was known as the creator and patron saint of Tai Chi Chuan. Innovation is the hidden message in the spiral motion of the Tai Chi Yin and Yang Symbol and it is one of the sources of Tai Chi Chuan’s creation. Today, we see innovation all around us, and the great strides that science and technology have made.

articles.content:
I. Introduction

Tai Chi Chuan, an internal Chinese martial art and health maintenance exercise is practicing by millions of people around the world today. Although there are many people practice it daily, there are very few people understanding its principles and attain any success from their practice, especially, there are many people spent their whole life on this. Everyone knows, after several hundred years of development, Tai Chi Chuan developed into many styles. Today, there are eight major styles of Tai Chi Chuan. They are Chen, Yang, Wu, Wu/Hao, Li, Sun, Zhaobao and the contemporary Wushu Styles such as the 24 Techniques Simplify Tai Chi Chuan, 48 Techniques Combination Tai Chi Chuan, and a series of International Competition Forms. Although executing the movements are differently, observing the principles and requirements such as slow, steady, circular motion, relaxation, continuity, coordination, empty and full differentiation, etc., are remaining the same.

One can see with popularization, "Tai Chi Chuan" became a trade name for a specific sport activity. A health maintenance exercise known by many people as a national treasure. "Tai Chi Chuan", to most of the people, it is a traditional Chinese culture and material art. However, to many people in China today, Tai Chi Chuan does not associate with Chinese martial art, most of the people in China practice it today are retiree, weakling and Wushu athletes. Tai Chi Chuan became an old people exercise, cheap and easy sport symbol. The systems that associate with Chinese martial arts are Shaolin System and southern boxing. Speaking objectively, the Tai Chi Chuan most of the people practice around the world is most likely Tai Chi calisthenics, not the traditional Tai Chi Chuan style as a martial art. It involves with groups of people practice in the parks in the morning with loud music. Most Tai Chi Chuan practitioners in China understood the health benefits and the rules for competition. They do not understand any information about the traditional Tai Chi Chuan’s extensive philosophical and practical principles, and its informative history.

II. The Separation guidelines

It does not matter how people interpreted the name “Tai Chi Chuan” today or what it is representing. What is the original meaning for Tai Chi Chuan? Tai Chi Chuan is a traditional Chinese martial art, no doubt. People have to pay attention to the fact that the history of Tai Chi Chuan came from the country side and made famous by Yang Lu Chan (1799-1872) in Beijing City in the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911). After three generations of propagation by the Yang Family members and their students. It is popular and known as an internal martial art and health maintenance exercise.

As the beginning of the Republic of China, Tai Chi Chuan is transforming from an internal Chinese martial art to a preventive health exercise and further developed into purely as a competition sport. This development strongly affected by the environment as well as social development and the advancement of humanity development.

Due to the fact that Tai Chi Chuan's development is divided into several stages and each stage is existing as the same timeline and continue to develop independently. With the acceptance from our society and practitioners, each stage of development became an independent identity.

In modern society, people appreciated multiple cultures. As the same time, with the trend of ageing people occupy a higher percentage of the population, there is a need for simpler and effective health exercise for them. Tai Chi Chuan is a good exercise without strenuous movement. It is suitable for all kind of people and it is simple and easy to promote. Therefore, traditional Tai Chi Chuan practitioners cannot and should not force everyone to practice Tai Chi Chuan the traditional way. There are many Tai Chi Chuan enthusiasts not interested the martial art aspect of the art. What they are interested in is the health benefit, the amusement, the graceful movements and the push hand exercise with a partner that is following all the rules. Therefore, there are many shorter and simpler routines developed so it is easier to learn, remember and practice. Traditional Tai Chi Chuan curriculum training involves very difficult and hard work with dedication. It has form, gong exercise and martial combat assimilation trainings. It required a long time and commitment to finish. Therefore, one can see that Tai Chi Chuan is developed into three major objectives. They are remaining as the traditional Chinese internal martial art; it developed into a health maintenance exercise and competition sport.

III. Recognizing the Three Objectives

Tai Chi Chuan has developed into three major objectives. Originally, Tai Chi Chuan was practiced among a small selected group of people. When Yang Lu Chan (1799-1872) entered Beijng City, China, it is the beginning of Tai Chi Chuan's popularization. After two hundred years of teaching, Tai Chi Chuan developed into many distinctive characteristics in theory, training method, practice and technique.

As a health maintenance exercise, it begins as the early Republic of China when more people moved into the city from the country sides. People such as Yang Cheng Fu (1883-1936) began to said that to improve the health and spirit of Chinese, one has to pick up martial art training. Yang Cheng Fu strongly recommended people should practice Tai Chi Chuan to improve their health and he modified the traditional solo form standard so that more people had access to learn, practice and benefit from it. With many people following this movement, Chinese martial art became the national art. Today, Tai Chi Chuan is accepted as one of the health maintenance exercise and stress management in mainland China and around the world. There are many well educated people participated in this campaign and published many theories, explanations, experiences and techniques on this subject.

In term of Tai Chi Chuan as a competition sport, it has established for several decades in China. Due to the necessary, there are many colleges and universities established school teams to completing, researching and teaching as a competition sport.

IV. Conclusion

Today, we clearly see Tai Chi Chuan developed into a martial art, health maintenance exercise and competition sport, the three major objectives with their own individual development. Tai Chi Chuan is like all traditional cultures. It is freely transmit on its’ own merit. Different people base on their understanding teach Tai Chi Chuan differently. There are people teaches Tai Chi Chuan as a martial art; there are people teaches Tai Chi Chuan as a health maintenance exercise and there are people teaches Tai Chi Chuan as a competition sport.

Tai Chi Chuan has three major objectives today is reflecting the multiple cultures phenomenon we have in our society. With this information, it is better for one to choose the correct objective when engaging in this Tai Chi Chuan journey.
